aryn_intro.title: The Water
aryn_intro.narrator: Aryn. Bearer of Water. What she remembers.
aryn_intro.text:
Water does not shout.

It waits.

It always finds its way.

I was five the first time I understood.

Not with my head.

With my hands.

choices.text: Water has always spoken to you.
You learned to listen to it.

aryn_enfance.title: The River
aryn_enfance.text:
We lived by the sea.

My father fished.
My mother mended nets.

I watched the water.

Every day.

Not because anyone asked me to.
Because the water watched me too.

I know that sounds strange.

But that's how it happened.

One morning, I put my hand in the river.

And the water stopped.

aryn_pouvoir.title: The Water That Stops
aryn_pouvoir.text:
Not the whole river.

Just the part under my hand.

A disc of still water.
Like glass.

I looked at it.

I pulled my hand away.

The water flowed on.

As if nothing had happened.

I was five.
I didn't tell anyone.

Water keeps secrets.
I could do the same.

aryn_secret.title: The Secret
aryn_secret.text:
Because I had seen how people looked at the different ones.

My village was small.
Like Cendral.

A boy could make faint illusions.
The adults avoided him.

A woman sometimes heard thoughts.
They drove her out one winter.

Ordinary magic was known.
Accepted in the big cities.

Less so here.

So I learned to keep the water inside me.

For two years.

choices.text: Did that solitude have a price?

aryn_decouverte_ordre.title: The Woman in Blue
aryn_decouverte_ordre.text:
I was seven when she came.

A woman.
Old.
Very old.

She wore blue.
The blue of the deep sea.

She stopped in front of me.

She didn't ask my name.
She didn't speak to my parents.

She just looked at my hands.

**"You've been keeping the water inside you for two years."**

It wasn't a question.

**"That must weigh on you."**

I cried.

I don't know why.
Just that someone knew.
And that it was an enormous relief.

choices.text: You had seen her in a dream.

aryn_recrutement.title: The Choice
aryn_recrutement.text:
She spoke with my parents.

For a long time.

I waited outside.

I caught fragments.

*The Order of the Blades.*
*A rare gift.*
*Aurenthal.*

My mother wept.

My father said nothing for a long while.

Then the door opened.

My mother held me tight.

**"You'll come back."** she said.

Not a question.
An order.

**"I promise."**

The woman in blue was waiting in the street.

**"Ready?"**

I was seven.
I didn't know what that meant.

**"Yes."**

aryn_aurenthal.title: Aurenthal
aryn_aurenthal.text:
Aurenthal was everything I had imagined.

And nothing I had imagined.

Big.
Loud.
Bright.

Magic everywhere.
Children making bubbles of light in the streets.
Merchants whose stalls floated.

And the Temple of the Order.

Tall.
Silent.
Unlike anything else.

At the entrance, three other children were waiting.

A boy with burns on his forearms.
A girl who smelled of earth after rain.
A boy who watched everything at once.

They watched me arrive.

The boy with the burns crossed his arms.

**"You're late."**

**"I just came from the coast."**

**"Everyone comes from somewhere."**

The girl who smelled of earth smiled.

**"Ignore him."**
**"He says that to everyone."**

choices.text: What was Ikar like at first?

aryn_premiers_jours.title: The First Days
aryn_premiers_jours.location: Temple of the Order — Training Hall
aryn_premiers_jours.text:
The first days were hard.

Not the training.
I loved the training.

But the spirits.

We couldn't really see them.
Shapes.
Voices.

The spirit of the former Bearer of Water.

Her name was Lyra.
She had died stopping Caël.

**"You must learn to let the water flow."** she would say.
**"Water doesn't force its way."**
**"It goes around."**
**"It waits."**
**"And it always gets through in the end."**

I loved Lyra.

Until she said something else.

aryn_ce_quils_ont_dit.title: What Lyra Said
aryn_ce_quils_ont_dit.text:
It was our third year.

We were ten.

Lyra kept me back after training.

The others had gone.

**"Aryn."**

**"Yes."**

**"The bearer of Chaos will come."**
**"You will know it."**
**"And when you know it..."**

She paused.

**"...you must be ready for anything."**

**"Like what..."**

**"Anything."**

Just that.

*Anything.*

I asked her what she meant.

She didn't answer.

She vanished the way spirits do.

I spent the night staring at the water in my basin.

The water didn't answer me either.

aryn_interpretation.title: What She Understood
aryn_interpretation.text:
I understood what everyone understood.

What the spirits meant.

The same thing our ancestors had done.

Stop the Chaos.

Even if it cost everything.

Ikar understood it first.

**"If we can't master it..."**
**"...we have to stop it."**

He said it without hesitation.
At ten years old.

Taera shook her head.

**"No."**
**"There has to be another way."**

Vael said nothing.
He smiled.
His smile for when he was truly thinking.

As for me, I kept silent.

Because I didn't know yet.

And water doesn't help people who don't know.

aryn_annees.title: The Years
aryn_annees.location: Temple of the Order — Different seasons
aryn_annees.text:
We grew up.

Our powers grew with us.

Ikar burned brighter.
Taera lifted boulders.
Vael vanished and reappeared.

I was learning to listen.

Water carries information.
Rivers know what happens upstream.
Rain knows where it came from.

I was learning to hear.

And the more I heard...
...the more the doubt grew.

Lyra watched me.

**"You doubt."**

**"Yes."**

**"Good."**

**"Good?"**

**"Doubt is water too."**
**"It goes around."**
**"It waits."**
**"It finds its way in the end."**

aryn_doute_detail.title: Aryn's Doubt
aryn_doute_detail.text:
I read everything the Order had on Caël.

Everything.

And I realized something.

The four sages of the time...

...they tried to kill him first.

Not to save him.
To kill him.

And it didn't work.

Because Chaos alone is stronger than any one of them.

It was only when they tried something else...
...when Taera — the former Taera — reached out her hand...
...that something changed.

Caël stopped.

Just for a second.

And that second was enough.

But the four died all the same.

Because they had waited too long.

*Ready for anything.*

Maybe that's what it meant.
Ready to reach out.
Even if it costs everything.

aryn_veille.title: The Signal
aryn_veille.location: Temple of the Order — Aryn's Room
aryn_veille.text:
We were nineteen.

It was evening.

I was in my room.

The basin of water on my table began to tremble.

Not from an earthquake.

From within.

Water trembling from within.

I knew what it meant.

I had waited twelve years for it.

I went to knock on Ikar's door.

He was already on his feet.
Dressed.
A blade at his belt.

**"You felt it too."**

**"Yes."**

**"To the west."**

**"Yes."**

We looked at each other.

Twelve years of training.

**"We warn the others."**

aryn_depart_ordre.title: The Departure
aryn_depart_ordre.text:
There were four of us in the courtyard.

The hour before dawn.

Taera gripped her sword.

Vael watched the western horizon.

**"You think it's him?"** Taera asked.

**"The water says yes."** I answered.

**"So does the fire."** said Ikar.

Vael nodded without turning around.

Lyra appeared.

She hadn't come to watch us leave in years.

She looked at us for a long moment.

**"Remember."**

**"All of it?"** Vael asked.

**"What matters."** she said.

And she vanished.

We mounted our horses.

aryn_route.title: The Road West
aryn_route.text:
We rode for a long time.

The road west.
Toward the borders.
Toward villages with no name on the great maps.

Ikar rode fast.
Always.

Taera watched every village we passed through.
As if she were searching for something.

Vael whistled.

I listened.

The water in the streams.
The rain in the clouds.
The dew on the grass.

Everything said the same thing.

*Farther.*
*Faster.*
*He's alone.*

choices.text: What else did the water say?

aryn_fumee.title: The Smoke
aryn_fumee.text:
We saw the smoke from a ridge.

Black.
Thick.
Far away.

Ikar stopped.

Taera closed her eyes.

Vael stopped whistling.

I watched the smoke.

And I thought of Lyra.

*Ready for anything.*

I had my answer now.

Not to kill.

To reach out.

Even if it costs everything.

**"Let's go."** I said.

No one answered.

We set off at a gallop.

choices.text: You think of him — not the Chaos. Him.

fin_memoire_aryn.title: Ending — Aryn's Memory
fin_memoire_aryn.text:
The memory fades.

Like water slipping through your fingers.

aryn_souvenir_eau.title: The Memory
aryn_souvenir_eau.text:
There's one thing I never say.

The sea spoke to me.

Not in words.

In images.

When I was little, I would fall asleep
and see things in the water.

People I didn't know.
Places I had never seen.

My mother thought I was daydreaming awake.

Maybe she was right.

Or maybe the water keeps the memory
of everything it has passed through.

And sometimes it lent it to me.

aryn_prix_secret.title: The Price of the Secret
aryn_prix_secret.text:
Yes.

There were nights when the water weighed on me.

Like something too heavy
in a pocket too small.

I dreamed I was overflowing.

That the water poured out of my eyes.
Out of my skin.
Out of my hair.

I woke up drenched in sweat.

And I looked at my hands in the dark.

Dry.

Nothing.

I fell back asleep.

The next day I began holding it in again.

aryn_pere.title: What Father Said
aryn_pere.text:
My father said nothing for a long time.

That was his way.
Fishermen know how to wait.

Then he laid his hand on my head.

**"The water always comes back."**

That was all.

He went back to mending his nets.

As if we had been talking about the weather.

My mother held me once more at the door.

She smelled of salt and wool.

I never caught that smell again afterward.

Not quite.

aryn_ikar_debut.title: Ikar — The First Days
aryn_ikar_debut.text:
Ikar annoyed me.

Not in a mean way.

Just that he had a way of taking up space.

Too direct.
Too sure.
Too much of everything.

In the second week he said:

**"Your water is too slow."**

**"That's the point."** I replied.

He frowned.

He didn't understand.

He said nothing.

Three days later, during training,
he put his blade in front of mine.

To block a strike I hadn't seen coming.

He never mentioned it.

Neither did I.

That's how we became friends.

aryn_esprits.title: The Spirits
aryn_esprits.location: Temple of the Order — Hall of the Elders
aryn_esprits.text:
The spirits were hard to look at.

Not because they frightened us.

Because they looked tired.

Lyra most of all.

Three hundred years guiding the Bearers of Water.
Waiting for the right moment.
Repeating the same lessons.

Once I asked her:

**"Do you want to leave?"**

She looked at me.

**"Leave where?"**

**"I don't know."**
**"Just... no longer be here."**

She thought for a long time.

**"When it's over."** she said.
**"Then I will leave."**

**"Over how?"**

She didn't answer.

I thought about that sentence for years.

aryn_taera_reaction.title: Taera's Reaction
aryn_taera_reaction.text:
Taera had wept that night.

I had heard her through the wall.

The next day she didn't mention it.

But during training,
when the spirit of Earth said
*"ready for anything"* a second time,

Taera said:

**"No."**

Just that.

Everyone stopped.

The spirit waited.

**"No, what?"**

**"No. I won't be ready for anything."**
**"There is always another way."**
**"You find it, or you just haven't looked hard enough."**

The spirit did not answer.

Vael looked at Taera.

With something in his eyes.

Respect, maybe.

Or recognition.

aryn_pensee_veille.title: What She Thought
aryn_pensee_veille.location: Temple of the Order — Aryn's Room
aryn_pensee_veille.text:
I thought of my father.

*The water always comes back.*

I thought of Lyra.

*When it's over, I will leave.*

I thought of Caël.

Not the monster of the legends.

The child who had received a prophecy
and who had been afraid.

Did he have people like us?

People who ran toward him
instead of fleeing?

I don't think so.

I think everyone fled.

And he was left alone with something
he didn't understand.

I didn't want that to happen again.

It was a simple thought.

But it was mine.

aryn_eau_route.title: What the Water Said
aryn_eau_route.text:
The water said he had been alone.

For a long time.

That the people around him were afraid.

That this fear came back to him like an echo.

And that the echo grew louder.

The water said something else too.

Something I had trouble hearing.

That he wanted us to stop him.

Not in the sense of killing him.

In the sense of calling out to him: *Stop.*

To be there.

To not run away like all the others.

I urged my horse faster.

aryn_eau_enfance_a.title: It Always Spoke
aryn_eau_enfance_a.text:
Not in words.

In sensations.

When a storm was coming, I knew before anyone.
Not because I watched the sky.
Because the water in the well changed taste.

My mother thought I was making it up.

My father said nothing.

Fishermen know the sea knows things.

They would rather not talk about it.

aryn_eau_enfance_b.title: Learning to Listen
aryn_eau_enfance_b.text:
At first I heard nothing.

Just water.
Noise.
Movement.

It began when I stayed still.

Not moving.
Not thinking.
Just being there.

Water speaks to people who wait.

That was the first lesson.
Before Lyra, even.
Before the Order.

The sea taught it to me on its own.

aryn_femme_reve.title: The Dream
aryn_femme_reve.text:
I had seen her.

Not clearly.
But a blue silhouette.
On the quay.

The night before she arrived.

The sea had shown me someone who was coming.

When she appeared in the square that morning,
I recognized the color before the face.

**"You were waiting for me."** she said.

**"Yes."**

She looked surprised.

Maybe the others hadn't expected it.

aryn_femme_peur.title: Fear
aryn_femme_peur.text:
She knew.

About the water in my hands.
About the dreams.
About everything I had kept secret.

She knew all of it just by looking at me.

It was terrifying.

Not because she was threatening.

Because it meant I had never really been alone.
That someone had been watching.
For how long?

I wanted to run.

But the water in the village well had begun to swirl gently.

As if to say:
stay.

aryn_doute_esprits.title: Doubting the Spirits
aryn_doute_esprits.text:
The spirits guided us.

But they had failed too.

Caël.

They had followed him. They had trained the four sages.
And the four sages had died.

Caël had nearly destroyed everything all the same.

How can you trust spirits
who had already made this mistake?

Lyra knew it.

**"You doubt us."** she told me once.

**"Yes."**

**"Good."** she replied.
**"The day you stop doubting us..."**
**"...is the day you will have stopped thinking."**

It was the first time I truly loved her.

aryn_doute_soi.title: Doubting Myself
aryn_doute_soi.text:
What if I was wrong?

What if the other way didn't exist?

What if Ikar had been right all along?

*Ready for anything.*

Maybe it meant exactly what it said.
No metaphor.
No interpretation.

Kill Chaos before it kills everything else.

On the nights when this doubt came,
I plunged my hands into the basin.

The water stayed cold.
Still.

The water did not give me the answer.

It only said:
*wait.*

I waited.

aryn_depart_ikar.title: Ikar's Gaze
aryn_depart_ikar.text:
Ikar was already in the saddle.

He was watching the western horizon.

Twelve years together.
Hundreds of training sessions.
Dozens of quarrels.

I knew exactly what he was thinking.

He wanted to get there before it was too late.

It wasn't violence.
It was fear.

Ikar had been afraid since he was ten years old,
when the spirit of Fire had said
*ready for anything.*

He had decided that meant yes.

And twelve years later
he still hadn't changed his mind.

I prayed for enough time
to make him change it.

aryn_depart_taera.title: Taera's Gaze
aryn_depart_taera.text:
Taera was looking at the temple.

She was no doubt remembering it.
The first time she had seen it.
Small. Her hands covered in earth.
Amazed that the others didn't feel what she felt.

She might never come back.

Or come back changed.

She caught my glance.

She just nodded.

No words.
We didn't need any.

Twelve years within the same walls.

Words had become almost superfluous.

aryn_depart_vael.title: Vael's Gaze
aryn_depart_vael.text:
Vael was whistling.

Of course.

Even now.

**"You're really whistling right now."** I said.

**"Always."**

**"Aren't you afraid?"**

He stopped whistling.

Just for a second.

**"Yes."**

He started again.

Louder this time.

Vael had understood something it had taken me years to learn.

Fear doesn't disappear when you pretend it isn't there.

But it takes up less room.

aryn_fumee_lui.title: Not the Chaos — Him
aryn_fumee_lui.text:
The legends spoke of the Chaos.

Not of a person.

But there, before that smoke,
I was thinking of someone.

Someone who had wanted to protect his village.

Someone who had been afraid.

Someone who did not know what he was.

Exactly like Caël.
Exactly like anyone
who discovers something too big inside themselves.

It was not the Chaos we would find in those ruins.

It was someone.

And someone can be reached.
Can be heard.

The water had told me so.

*He wanted us to be there.*

aryn_fumee_cendral.title: Cendral
aryn_fumee_cendral.text:
A village.

Like mine.

People who got up in the morning.
Who baked their bread.
Who watched their children grow.

And now, smoke.

Because of a power that one person had not chosen.

I thought of my mother.
*You'll come back.*

I thought of my father.
*The water always comes back.*

I thought of Lyra.
*When it's over, I will leave.*

All these people who had told me something important
without really knowing it.

I hoped I would live up to what they had handed down to me.
